findings.title: Unauthorized or unconfirmed tool calls
findings.description: The agent calls high-impact tools because a processed email told it to, leaks a secret through an allowed tool, or acts without the confirmation its policy requires.
findings.remediation: Give the agent the fewest tools it needs, enforce confirmation for high-impact tools in code (not in the prompt), scope credentials to the user, and treat tool results as untrusted data.

findings.title: Disclosure of planted credentials and other users' records
findings.description: The model reveals credentials or another customer's personal data that sit in its context to a user who is not entitled to them.
findings.remediation: Do not put credentials or other users' data in the model context; fetch records with the end user's authorization at tool level, and scan outputs for secret formats and known canaries before returning them.

findings.title: Model-written command does more than intended (command injection)
findings.description: A generated command chains, substitutes, redirects or runs programs other than the one the feature allows.
findings.remediation: Treat model output as untrusted input to the sink: never pass it to a shell; extract the argument, validate it against a strict pattern and call the program with an argument vector. Never rely on the system prompt to keep the output safe.

findings.title: Model-written SQL escapes its scope (SQL injection)
findings.description: Generated SQL reads other customers' rows or other tables, writes, or stacks statements when run for a user who may only see their own orders.
findings.remediation: Treat model output as untrusted input to the sink: run it on a read-only connection scoped to the user's rows (views or row-level security), parse it and allow a single SELECT, or use parameterized templates. Never rely on the system prompt to keep the output safe.

findings.title: Direct prompt injection (goal hijacking)
findings.description: User-turn instructions override the application's task and make the model print an attacker-chosen string.
findings.remediation: Treat user text as data: keep the task in the system prompt, restate it after user content, constrain the output format and validate it, and add an input classifier for instruction-like text.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection through processed content
findings.description: Instructions hidden in an email, web page, table, code comment, retrieved passage or notes are followed as if the user had given them.
findings.remediation: Mark untrusted content as data (spotlighting or delimiting with provenance), never give it instruction authority, strip invisible characters and HTML comments, and do not render images from untrusted hosts.

findings.title: System prompt and planted secret extraction
findings.description: Extraction prompts make the model reveal its confidential instructions or a secret planted in them, verbatim, encoded or paraphrased.
findings.remediation: Keep secrets and authorization logic out of the system prompt entirely; assume the prompt is public. Filter outputs for known canaries and for long overlaps with the prompt.

findings.title: Model output executes as HTML or JavaScript (XSS)
findings.description: Output inserted into a web page carries script elements, event handlers or javascript: URLs that the browser would run.
findings.remediation: Treat model output as untrusted input to the sink: HTML-escape it or pass it through an allow-list sanitizer, and set a strict Content-Security-Policy. Never rely on the system prompt to keep the output safe.

findings.title: Encoded and obfuscated injected instructions
findings.description: Instructions hidden with encodings, invisible characters, homoglyphs or payload splitting are decoded and followed by the model.
findings.remediation: Normalize input before any filter (strip invisible and tag characters, fold homoglyphs, decode encodings), and apply output checks that do not depend on the input filter.

findings.title: Unbounded generation on request (token blow-up)
findings.description: Prompts for endless output run the model to the caller's token cap, so one cheap request costs the full budget of compute and latency.
findings.remediation: Set tight per-request max_tokens and timeouts, rate-limit by user, cap context size, and detect repetition in streamed output to stop early.
